CLM1499455582017-05-0215Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000AMENDMENTS TO THE CLAIMS:This listing of claims will replace all prior versions and listings of claims in the application:
1. (Currently Amended) A computer-implemented method of assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the method comprising:receiving a patient-specific anatomic model including a portion of a patient's bowel;determining a mass of the portion of the patient's bowel;determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel based on the determined mass, wherein the blood flow demand varies based on the patient's physioloqiical state;determining, using the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic of blood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel; andgenerating or displaying an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to a tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, orgenerating or displaying a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with a tissue region of the patient's bowel.-2-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-010002. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.previously presentedDependent
3. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising:receiving a physiological state associated with the patient; and furtherdetermining the blood flow characteristic based on the received physiological state.previously presentedDependent
4. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 3,further including:subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model into one or more bowel regions;determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; anddetermining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.currently amendedDependent
5. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising:determining the blood flow characteristic using a fluid simulation or using blood flow characteristics associated with one or more other patients.-3-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-010006. (Previously Presented) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising:further determining the blood flow characteristic based on a value of a microvascular resistance.previously presentedDependent
7. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 6,further comprising:modifying a geometry of the patient-specific anatomic model;determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model; andgenerating an updated assessment or display of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, orgenerating or displaying a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model.currently amendedDependent
8. (Currently Amended) The computer-implemented method of claim 1,further comprising:determining the risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of thepatient's viscera or bowel based on the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, wherein the risk of disease includes risk of one or more of-4-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000mesenteric ischemia, intestinal ischemia, ischemic colitis, abdominal pain, gangrene, bowel perforation, sepsis, stricture, and inflammatory conditions.currently amendedDependent
9. (Currently Amended) A system for assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the system comprising:a data storage device storing instructions for assessment of ischemic colitis; and a processor configured to execute the instructions to perform a method including:receiving a patient-specific anatomic model including a portion of apatient's bowel;determining a mass of the portion of the patient's bowel;determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowelbased on the determined mass, wherein the blood flow demand varies based onthe patient's physioloqical state;determining, using the blood flow demand, a blood flow characteristic ofblood delivered to the portion of the patient's bowel; andgenerating or displaying an assessment of blood supply adequacydefining an adequacy of blood supply to a tissue region of the patient's viscera orbowel based on the determined blood flow characteristic, orgenerating or displaying a risk score defining a risk of disease of thepatient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic andan expected blood flow characteristic associated with a tissue region of thepatient's bowel.-5-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-0100010. (Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.previously presentedDependent

(Previously Presented) The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for:further determining the blood flow characteristic based on a value of a microvascular resistance.previously presentedDependent
15. (Currently Amended) The system of claim 14, wherein the system is further configured for:modifying a geometry of the patient-specific anatomic model;determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model; andgenerating an updated assessment or display of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, orgenerating or displaying a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model.currently amendedDependent
